item.title: Cloud API
item.description:
To create integrations, retrieve data, and automate your cloud native infrastructure, build with the Layer5 Cloud REST API.

Every endpoint lives under /api on the host of your Layer5 Cloud deployment. Hosted Layer5 Cloud uses https://cloud.layer5.io/api. A self-hosted deployment uses https://<your-cloud-host>/api.

Authenticating with the API 🔗

In order to authenticate to Layer5 Cloud’s REST API, you need to generate and use a security token. Visit your user account’s security tokens and generate a long-lived token. Security tokens remain valid until you revoke them, and you can issue as many as you need.

item.title: Reference
item.description:
These pages state facts about Layer5 Cloud: which plan includes a capability, which role holds a permission, and how to call the REST API. Start with Concepts for how the pieces fit together.

Page Use it to
Default Permissions Find out which default role holds a permission in the permission list.
Keys See how a key reaches a user, which security keys the server enforces, and the key endpoints.
Keychains See who can change a keychain and the keychain endpoints.
Sessions Check session lifetimes, cookies, and how to sign out a session.
Tokens Create, list, rotate, and revoke API tokens.
Cloud API Authenticate, set the organization, page through results, and handle errors.

Security permission keys 🔗

Provider Admin holds every key. The table lists the default holders of the other roles, as of Layer5 Cloud v1.0.280. “Interface” means the control or tab is disabled or replaced by a permission error screen. “Server” means the Layer5 Cloud server refuses the request with HTTP 403.
